source_section: 6.1 TCS — Tax Collected at Source (GST, Section 52)
summary: 6.1 TCS — Tax Collected at Source (GST, Section 52) TCS is collected by Snapdeal under Section 52 of CGST Act 2017 at 1% of net taxable value (0.5% CGST + 0.5% SGST for intra-state; 1% IGST for inter-state). In the dataset, TCS entries appear in snapdealsettlement as: TCS-COD Vendor Invoice — TCS on COD forward orders TCS-NCOD Vendor Invoice — TCS on prepaid orders TCS-COD Return to Vendor — TCS reversal on returns TCS-COD RTS to Vendor — TCS reversal on RTS

source_section: 6.2 TDS — Tax Deducted at Source (Income Tax, Section 194-O)
summary: 6.2 TDS — Tax Deducted at Source (Income Tax, Section 194-O) TDS is deducted by Snapdeal at 1% of gross sales under Section 194-O of the Income Tax Act (effective from October 1, 2020). 1. Table Overview snapdealnonorder captures non-order financial adjustments — transactions that are linked to a sub-order but are not order charges themselves. In the current dataset, this table exclusively contains TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) entries: per-order TDS deductions applied by Snapdeal under Income Tax provisions. Every COD and NCOD order that qualifies for TDS generates a corresponding entry in this table. The grossamount is typically a small negative value (−₹0.13 to −₹0.25 per order), representing the TDS deducted from the seller's settlement. This table is important for income tax reconciliation — sellers can use these entries to claim TDS credit when filing their IT returns.…

5. Understanding TDS on Marketplace Transactions

TDS Framework (Income Tax Act, Section 194-O) Section 194-O (inserted by Finance Act 2020) mandates e-commerce operators to deduct TDS at 1% on the gross amount of sales facilitated through their platform for Indian sellers. This applies when: The seller has a PAN The gross sales exceed ₹5 lakh per financial year Rate: 1% of gross order value (0.5% if PAN not available — 2% prior to amendments) In the data: TDS amounts are typically ₹0.13–₹0.25 per order On an order of ₹176 (avg chargedamount), 1% TDS ≈ ₹1.76 — the small amounts suggest these may be per-item or partial TDS entries Snapdeal deducts and deposits TDS on behalf of sellers; sellers get credit via Form 26AS

1. Table Overview snapdealpayments is the bank remittance / payment confirmation table for Snapdeal. It records the actual cash transfers made by Snapdeal to the seller's registered bank account. Each row represents one payment event — a NEFT/RTGS wire from Snapdeal to the seller — identified by a UTR (Unique Transaction Reference) number. This table is the smallest in the pipeline and serves as the final reconciliation anchor: the grossamount here should match the sum of settledamount in snapdealsettlement for the same payment batch. Matching UTR numbers between this table and snapdealsettlement.settlementid closes the payment loop. > Pipeline Note: As of April 2025, zsobserve.snapdealpayme…

UTR Number Format The UTR numbers follow HDFC NEFT/RTGS format: Pattern: HDFCN5YYYYMMDD{9-digit-sequence} Example: HDFCN52025030699811073 Bank: HDFC (HDFC) Channel: NEFT (N5) Date: 20250306 (March 6, 2025) Sequence: 99811073 This UTR maps to settlementid in snapdealsettlement for payment batch matching. ---

6. Payment Cycle Analysis Snapdeal's payment cycle for sellers is typically weekly (7+N days after delivery). Based on observed data: Payments occur approximately every 2–4 days for active sellers Settlement IDs in snapdealsettlement use the same UTR format as utrno here The single bank account (Payment-HDFC-1809) indicates one consolidated seller bank account registered with Snapdeal ---
